en: Now put it in the Earth-centred frame and SEE the trip. From a low parking orbit you fire the trans-lunar injection at perigee and coast a long half-ellipse whose far end (apogee) just reaches the Moon's distance — a roughly five-day fall uphill. But you do not aim AT the Moon: it moves about 62° along its orbit while you coast, so you aim where it WILL be and arrive as it catches up. At the far end you fire again to be captured into lunar orbit. Both Δv here are the real patched-conic values from the kernel's Earth-Moon Lambert solver — this is the geometry every crewed lunar mission from Apollo to Artemis flies.
cur: 现在切换到地心参考系，直观感受整个旅程。从低停泊轨道出发，你在近地点点火进行月球转移轨道注入，随后沿一条漫长的半椭圆滑行，其远端（远地点）恰好触及月球距离——这是一段约五天的爬坡下落。但你并不瞄准月球本身：在你滑行期间它沿轨道移动约62°，因此你要瞄准它将要到达的位置，在它追上时抵达。在远端你再次点火，被月球捕获进入环月轨道。此处两次Δv均为内核地月Lambert求解器给出的真实拼接圆锥曲线值——从Apollo到Artemis，每一次载人登月任务飞行的都是这套几何。

en: Patched-conic insertion (instantaneous sphere-of-influence handover)
cur: 拼接圆锥曲线入轨（瞬时影响球范围交接）

en: Underpowered for this payload — the stack runs out of Δv before orbital speed. Lighten the payload or lower the orbit.
cur: 对该有效载荷动力不足——箭体在达到轨道速度前就耗尽了 Δv。请减轻有效载荷或降低轨道高度。

en: Planar (2-D) ascent, eastward launch, single-exponential atmosphere
cur: 平面（2-D）上升，向东发射，单指数大气

en: Launching gets you UP; orbit is going sideways fast enough that you keep missing the ground — about 7.8 km/s. But climbing through gravity and air, a real rocket pays a tax that pushes the true cost past 9 km/s. Let's fly it for real.
cur: 发射让你升上去；轨道则是横向飞得足够快，快到你不断错过地面——大约7.8 km/s。但穿越引力与大气爬升时，真实的火箭要缴一笔税，把实际代价推到9 km/s以上。让我们真刀真枪地飞一次。

en: First, the target. Orbit is a SPEED, not a height: at ~200 km you must be moving ~7.8 km/s sideways, or you fall back down. Height alone is nothing — a sub-orbital hop reaches space and drops straight back. The whole game is the horizontal speed.
cur: 首先看目标。轨道是一种速度，而非高度：在约 200 km 高度，你必须横向移动约 7.8 km/s，否则就会坠落。仅有高度毫无意义——亚轨道跳跃触及太空后便直接落回。全部关键在于横向速度。

en: Now fly it. This runs the real ascent — the same gravity-turn integrator our mission screens use — and breaks out the three taxes a textbook Δv hides: GRAVITY loss (thrust burned holding the rocket up while it climbs), DRAG loss (the atmosphere), and STEERING loss (the cosine cost of tilting from vertical toward horizontal). Add them to the 7.8 km/s of orbital speed and you get the ~9.4 km/s every launch vehicle is really sized for. Load it heavier and watch the same rocket fall short — orbit is a knife-edge of mass.
cur: 现在起飞。这运行真实上升——与我们任务屏幕使用的相同的重力转向积分器——并分解出教科书Δv隐藏的三项损耗：重力损耗（克服火箭在上升时保持火箭抬升所需的推力消耗）、阻力损耗（大气层）和姿态调整损耗（从竖直向水平倾斜产生的余弦代价）。将它们加到轨道速度的7.8 km/s，你就得到每个发射器真正设计所需的~9.4 km/s。加重它，看同一枚火箭如何达不到轨道——轨道是质量的刀刃。

en: Everything in space starts here: you cannot go to the Moon, Mars, or anywhere until you are first in orbit — moving fast enough sideways to keep falling around the Earth. Sputnik proved it in 1957; four years later Gagarin rode the same idea to become the first human in orbit.
cur: 太空中的一切都从这里开始：在你首先进入轨道之前——即横向移动足够快以持续绕地球坠落——你无法前往月球、火星或任何地方。Sputnik 在 1957 年证明了这一点；四年后加加林凭同一原理成为首位进入轨道的人类。

en: Newton drew it in 1687: a cannon on a mountain fired harder and harder, until the ball falls exactly as fast as the Earth curves away and never lands. That is orbit — perpetual falling.
cur: Newton 于 1687 年描绘了它：山顶上的大炮越打越猛，直到炮弹坠落的速度恰好与地球弯曲远去的速度相同，便永不落地。那就是轨道——永恒的坠落。

en: You are in orbit. Now you can go somewhere — to the Moon, to Mars, or catch another spacecraft already up here.
cur: 你已在轨道上。现在你可以前往某处了——月球、火星，或去追赶另一艘已在此处的航天器。

en: PEG linear-tangent steering (sin γ = A + B·t) with a per-cycle gravity integral
cur: PEG 线性正切制导（sin γ = A + B·t），每周期进行一次重力积分

en: There is physics, and then there are problems the physics makes too HARD to solve by hand — and reaching orbit is one. The first lesson on the guidance computers that fly the machine, not the physics they obey.
cur: 有物理学，也有一些被物理学弄得太难、无法手算的问题——入轨就是其一。这是关于制导计算机的第一课：它们驾驶机器，而非它们所遵循的物理。

en: Watch the flight computer think. Getting to orbit is a boundary-value problem with an exact answer — arrive at the target altitude, going level, at circular speed — and the vehicle's real state drifts every second, so you cannot pre-plan the whole path. So it flies in two regimes. In the thick atmosphere it follows a PRE-PLANNED pitch table (open-loop) that keeps the loads safe through the gravity turn. Above ~55 km the computer TAKES OVER: for this low-thrust upper stage that is Powered Explicit Guidance, which re-solves a two-point boundary problem each second for a steering law sin γ = A + B·t — and its answer LOFTS the climb, commanding the nose BELOW the horizon to spend altitude buying speed. No human flies that blind. Lower the upper-stage thrust and watch it loft harder.
cur: 观察飞行计算机如何“思考”。进入轨道是一个有精确解的边界值问题——在目标高度、水平飞行、达到圆轨道速度——而飞行器的实际状态每秒都在漂移，所以无法预先规划整条路径。因此它分两个阶段飞行。在稠密大气中，它遵循一张预先规划的俯仰表（开环），通过重力转向保证载荷安全。在约 55 km 以上，计算机接管：对于这个低推力上面级，采用的是动力显式制导，它每秒重新求解一次两点边界问题，得到操纵律 sin γ = A + B·t——其解会让爬升“抬高”，指令机头指向地平线下方，以消耗高度来换取速度。没有人能这样盲飞。降低上面级推力，看它抬得更高。

en: Every launch vehicle since the 1960s has flown itself the last stretch to orbit, because the insertion is too precise and too fast for a human hand. The Apollo Guidance Computer ran exactly this kind of closed-loop steering on 4 KB of memory; today Falcon 9's computer does it and then lands the booster on a boat — control problems no person could solve in real time.
cur: 自 1960 年代以来，每一枚运载火箭在入轨前的最后一段都是自主飞行的，因为入轨对人手来说太精确、太快。Apollo Guidance Computer 在 4 KB 内存上运行的正是这种闭环制导；如今 Falcon 9 的计算机做同样的事，还能把助推器降落在海上驳船上——这些控制问题没有人能实时求解。

en: Draper's MIT lab bet the Moon on it: the Apollo Guidance Computer was the first machine to fly humans, steering by re-solving its own guidance equations many times a second — the ancestor of every fly-by-wire system since.
cur: Draper 的 MIT 实验室为此押上了登月成败：Apollo Guidance Computer 是第一台驾驭载人飞行的机器，通过每秒多次重解自己的制导方程来操纵飞行——是此后每一套电传飞控系统的鼻祖。

en: You have met the ascent computer. The same idea — a machine solving a control problem too hard for a human — runs the powered descent to a landing and the lift-vector steering through a re-entry corridor.
cur: 你已认识了上升计算机。同样的思路——机器求解人类难以应对的控制问题——也支配着着陆的动力下降，以及再入走廊中的升力矢量制导。

en: Apollo 11 — flown by the Apollo Guidance Computer
cur: Apollo 11 — 由 Apollo Guidance Computer 驾驭

en: Saturn V — the Instrument Unit that steered it
cur: Saturn V——操纵它的仪器舱

en: Falcon 9 — flies to orbit and lands itself
cur: Falcon 9——自主入轨并自主着陆

en: Crashed — arrived too fast for the braking to null the velocity before the surface. Slow the approach or raise the max braking.
cur: 坠毁——抵达速度过快，制动无法在触及地表前将速度归零。请放缓接近速度或提高最大制动。

en: Vertical descent, throttle back-solved from the descent-rate schedule
cur: 垂直下降，节流阀由下降率计划反解得出

en: Constant surface gravity (low-altitude approximation)
cur: 恒定地表重力（低空近似）

en: On a world with no air you cannot parachute down — the only brake is the engine. A burn that must stop you at exactly zero altitude, with seconds of fuel to spare, is a control loop no human flies by eye. Here you fly the real one.
cur: 在没有空气的世界，你无法靠降落伞下降——唯一的刹车是发动机。一次必须让你恰好在零高度停下、且只剩几秒燃料余量的点火，是任何人都无法凭肉眼驾驭的控制回路。在这里，你驾驶那真实的一环。

en: A soft landing is a race between altitude and speed. The controller runs a descent-rate SCHEDULE — the target speed is proportional to how high you still are (v = gain·altitude), so it eases you toward a crawl as the ground rises to meet you — and it throttles the engine every step to track that line, rate-limited so the g never spikes. Fly it: from a couple of kilometres up, watch the computer null your speed to a gentle touchdown. Then arrive faster, or cap the braking lower, and watch the same computer run out of room — the speed stays above the schedule all the way down and you hit hard. This is the loop Apollo's lunar module, the Mars sky-crane, and every Falcon 9 booster landing flies.
cur: 软着陆是高度与速度之间的赛跑。控制器运行一套下降率计划——目标速度与你剩余高度成正比（v = 增益·高度），因此随着地面迎面升起，它引导你逐渐趋于缓行——并在每一步调节发动机节流以跟踪该线，且限制变化率以防 g 值骤增。来飞飞看：从几公里高处，看着计算机将你的速度归零，实现温和触地。然后以更快速度抵达，或将制动上限设得更低，看着同一台计算机耗尽余地——速度一路都高于计划线，你将重重撞地。这正是Apollo 登月舱、火星空中吊车以及每一次 Falcon 9 助推器着陆所运行的回路。

en: You cannot hand-fly a rocket to a soft touchdown: the throttle has to be trimmed many times a second to null the velocity at the instant of contact, and being a few percent off means a crater. Every soft landing on another world — Luna 9, the Apollo LM, Curiosity, Perseverance — and every Falcon 9 return has been flown by a computer running exactly this kind of terminal-guidance loop.
cur: 你无法手动驾驶火箭实现软着陆：节流阀必须每秒调整许多次，才能在接触瞬间将速度归零，而偏差哪怕几个百分点都会留下一个坑。在其他天体上的每一次软着陆——Luna 9、Apollo LM、Curiosity、Perseverance——以及每一次 Falcon 9 返回，都由运行着正是这种末端制导回路的计算机来完成。

en: Apollo 11's landing computer threw 1202 alarms while overloaded, and kept flying the descent anyway — because its guidance loop was designed to shed low-priority work and never drop the one job that mattered: land the spacecraft. Armstrong took manual attitude control, but the computer still ran the throttle.
cur: Apollo 11的着陆计算机在过载时抛出了 1202 报警，却依然继续飞完下降——因为它的制导回路被设计成能舍弃低优先级工作，而绝不放弃那唯一要紧的任务：让飞船着陆。阿姆斯特朗接管了姿态手动控制，但节流阀仍由计算机运行。

en: You have flown the landing computer. One control loop is left — steering the LIFT of a capsule through the knife-edge re-entry corridor.
cur: 你已驾驭了着陆计算机。只剩下一个控制回路——操纵返回舱的升力穿越那刀锋般的再入走廊。

en: This entry does not survive — too steep (over-g) or too shallow (skipped out). It sits outside the survivable corridor.
cur: 此次再入无法生还——太陡（过载超限）或太浅（弹跳飞出）。它落在可生还走廊之外。

en: 2-D lifting entry (altitude, speed, flight-path angle), exponential atmosphere, constant-g bank law
cur: 2-D lifting entry（高度、速度、航迹角），指数大气模型，恒加速度倾斜率律

en: Coming home from the Moon at 11 km/s, a capsule cannot throttle and cannot open a parachute — its only control is to ROLL, aiming its lift up or down. Fly that control and see what it buys you: a corridor.
cur: 以11 km/s从月球归来，返回舱既不能调节推力，也不能打开降落伞——它唯一的操控是滚转，让升力朝上或朝下。驾驭这一操控，看看它换来了什么：一条走廊。

en: Recall the ballistic corridor: too steep and you are crushed, too shallow and you skip back into space — and for a lunar return a plummeting capsule has almost no gap between the two. Lift is the way out. A capsule with a little lift can BANK to steer: roll so the lift points up and it pulls out of a steep dive (capping the g); roll so it points down and it digs into a shallow one (stopping the skip). This lesson flies a real lifting entry with a bank controller holding the deceleration, then sweeps every entry angle to measure the survivable corridor. A ballistic capsule's is a knife-edge; even Apollo's modest lift-to-drag of 0.3 roughly DOUBLES it. Turn up the lift-to-drag and watch the corridor widen — the margin that made crewed Moon returns survivable.
cur: 回想那条弹道走廊：太陡你会被压垮，太浅你会弹回太空——而对于月球返回，急坠的返回舱在两者之间几乎没有余地。升力就是出路。带有少许升力的返回舱可以通过滚转来操控：滚转使升力指向上方，它便能从陡降中拉起（限制g载荷）；滚转使升力指向下方，它便能扎进浅弹道中（阻止弹跳）。本课操控一次真实的升力再入，用滚转控制器保持减速度，随后扫过每一个再入角以测量可生还走廊。弹道返回舱的走廊窄如刀刃；即便Apollo那不高的0.3升阻比也大约将其扩大一倍。调高升阻比，看着走廊变宽——正是这份余量让载人月球返回得以生还。

en: Every crew that has come back from the Moon — Apollo, and soon Artemis — rode a LIFTING capsule that banked to steer through a re-entry corridor a ballistic craft could never thread. The Apollo command module rolled left and right under computer control the whole way down, its offset centre of mass giving just enough lift to hold the g-load and reach the recovery zone.
cur: 每一批从月球返回的乘员——Apollo，以及即将到来的Artemis——乘坐的都是升力返回舱，通过滚转穿越一条弹道飞行器绝无法穿过的再入走廊。Apollo指令舱在整个下降过程中都在计算机控制下左右滚转，其偏置质心提供了恰好够用的升力，以保持g载荷并抵达回收区。

en: Apollo's computer flew re-entry as a bank program: it commanded roll reversals — flip the lift left, then right — to steer downrange while holding the deceleration, threading a corridor about two degrees wide at 40,000 km/h. Bank wrong and you skip off into a lonely orbit or burn.
cur: Apollo的计算机将再入作为一套滚转程序来飞行：它指令滚转反转——先把升力翻向左，再翻向右——以在保持减速度的同时操控航程，在40,000 km/h时穿过一条约两度宽的走廊。滚转出错，你就会弹入孤独的轨道或被烧毁。

en: That is all three flight computers — the ascent guidance, the landing throttle, and the re-entry bank. Together they fly a whole mission no human hand could.
cur: 这就是全部三台飞行计算机——上升制导、着陆推力、再入滚转。它们合力完成一整趟任何人手都无法飞行的任务。

en: Apollo 11 — the lifting command-module re-entry
cur: Apollo 11——升力指令舱再入

en: Orion — the lifting capsule for Artemis returns
cur: Orion——用于Artemis返回的升力返回舱

en: OSIRIS-REx — a lifting sample-return entry
cur: OSIRIS-REx——一次升力样本返回再入

en: The whole journey in one notebook — launch, translunar coast, landing, and the ride home. Retrace Apollo end to end and watch every phase connect.
cur: 整段旅程尽在一册笔记——发射、地月转移滑行、着陆与返航。从头到尾重走Apollo，看每个阶段如何环环相扣。

en: Every Moon shot starts the same way: reach orbit. The Saturn V upper stage cannot be flown by hand — a guidance computer (PEG) solves its own steering in real time, pitching the stack to arrive at the exact speed and height for low Earth orbit. This is the first of the three computers that fly this mission.
cur: 每一次登月都以同样的方式开始：进入轨道。土星五号上面级无法手动飞行——制导计算机（PEG）实时解算自身的转向，调整整个箭体的俯仰角，以精确的速度和高度抵达近地轨道。这是执行本次任务的三台计算机中的第一台。

en: In orbit you do not aim at the Moon — you aim at where it will be. One burn (trans-lunar injection, TLI) stretches your orbit into an ellipse that reaches lunar distance; the coast takes about three days (the minimum-energy transfer here runs a little longer — Apollo spent fuel to fly it faster), then a second burn (lunar orbit insertion, LOI) brakes you into orbit around the Moon.
cur: 在轨道上你并不瞄准月球——你瞄准它将要到达的位置。一次点火（月球转移入轨，TLI）把你的轨道拉伸成一个抵达月球距离的椭圆；滑行约需三天（这里的最小能量转移会稍长一些——Apollo 消耗燃料以更快飞行），随后第二次点火（月球轨道入轨，LOI）将你制动进入环月轨道。

en: The landing computer takes over. After a burn cancels most of your orbital speed, it flies a descent-rate schedule for the final approach — throttling the engine every moment so you ease to a crawl exactly as the ground rises to meet you. No air, no parachute: thrust is the only brake. (This rung models that final powered descent, not the full orbit-cancel burn.)
cur: 着陆计算机接管。一次点火抵消大部分轨道速度后，它为最终进近执行一套下降率程序——每时每刻调节推力，让你在地面迎面升起的那一刻恰好减速到蠕行。没有空气，没有降落伞：推力是唯一的刹车。（这一环节模拟的是最终动力下降，而非完整的轨道抵消点火。）

en: Now leave. The ascent stage fires and climbs back to lunar orbit. With no atmosphere there is no drag and no steering loss — the whole Δv goes into speed, which is why a small ascent stage is enough to leave the Moon.
cur: 现在离开。上升级点火，重新爬升回月球轨道。没有大气，就没有阻力，也没有转向损失——全部 Δv 都转化为速度，这正是一个小小的上升级就足以离开月球的原因。

en: One more burn throws you home: trans-Earth injection (TEI). By symmetry it is the SAME cislunar ellipse run in reverse — so the transfer numbers match the outbound leg — a burn out of lunar orbit onto a coast that falls back to Earth.
cur: 再一次点火把你抛回家：地球转移入轨（TEI）。由对称性，它就是同一条地月椭圆的反向运行——所以转移参数与去程一致——一次从月球轨道出发的点火，进入一段坠回地球的滑行。

en: The climax. You hit the atmosphere at nearly 11 km/s — coming from the Moon, not just from orbit. Flown ballistic, the survivable corridor almost vanishes: too shallow and you skip back into space, too steep and the g-load is fatal. That is why the capsule flies LIFTING — the entry computer banks its offset lift vector up and down, and that lift roughly DOUBLES the survivable corridor. The bars here compare the two: lift is the difference between a splashdown and a burn-up.
cur: 高潮时刻。你以近 11 km/s 的速度冲入大气层——这是从月球返回，而非仅从轨道再入。若采用弹道式再入，可生存的走廊几乎消失：太浅会被弹回太空，太陡则过载致命。这正是舱体采用升力式再入的原因——再入计算机让偏置升力矢量上下滚转，这份升力能将可生存走廊大致翻倍。这里的柱状图对比二者：升力就是溅落与烧毁之间的分界。

en: A Moon mission is not one problem — it is a chain of them, each a different regime with a different machine to fly it. This capstone walks the whole Apollo 8 round trip end to end, so every rung you learned separately clicks into one flight.
cur: 登月任务不是一个问题——而是一连串问题，每一段都是不同的飞行阶段，需要用不同的机器来驾驭。这个综合项目将Apollo 8的整个往返之旅从头到尾走一遍，让你分别学到的每一个环节汇聚成一次完整的飞行。

en: Apollo 8 flew this round trip in December 1968 — the first crew to orbit the Moon and ride an 11 km/s lifting entry home. (Its return is at /fly?mission=apollo8; note our fixed-lift model flies a fuller exo-atmospheric skip than the flown in-atmosphere loft.)
cur: Apollo 8 于 1968 年 12 月完成了这次往返——首个进入环月轨道并以 11 km/s 升力式再入返回的乘组。（其返程见 /fly?mission=apollo8；请注意我们的固定升力模型飞出的是比实际大气内上举更完整的大气外跳跃。）

en: Target is outside the reachable footprint — the computer clamps to the nearest edge (flown at full lift-up or full lift-down).
cur: 目标超出可达落区范围——计算机将其限制到最近的边缘（以全升力向上或全升力向下飞行）。

en: Surviving the corridor is only half the job — the computer must also land you at the recovery zone, not just anywhere. Downrange is monotone in bank: full lift-up flies the farthest (a long shallow skim), lift-down digs in short. So the computer solves the one bank angle that lands at your target. The footprint curve shows the price: a near target forces a lift-down dig-in that spikes the g, a far one rides lift-up gently. Range and g trade — and the computer hits both.
cur: 熬过再入走廊只是任务的一半——计算机还必须让你着陆在回收区，而不是随便哪里。航程随倾侧角单调变化：全升力向上飞得最远（长而浅的掠飞），升力向下则短促下扎。因此计算机解算出唯一能落在目标点的倾侧角。落区范围曲线揭示了代价：近距目标迫使升力向下下扎，使g值飙升，远距目标则平缓地借助升力向上。航程与g此消彼长——而计算机两者兼顾。

en: Your rebound clears this world's escape velocity — there is no apex to report. You didn't land; you left.
cur: 你的反弹速度超过了这个天体的逃逸速度——没有顶点可报告。你没有着陆；你逃离了。

en: Uses the body's mean radius — real small worlds are lumpy, and local gravity varies across their surface.
cur: 使用天体平均半径——真实的小天体表面不规则，各处的重力不同。

en: Vertical rebound along the local radius; rotation and sideways motion are ignored.
cur: 沿当地竖直方向反弹；忽略自转和横向运动。

en: Gravity so weak you could jump clean off. On a comet or asteroid, landing is less a descent than a slow, careful docking with a mountain in space.
cur: 引力弱到你一跳就能脱离。在彗星或小行星上，着陆与其说是下降，不如说是与一座太空中的山峰缓慢而谨慎地对接。

en: Comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko is a mountain-sized world where gravity is a rumour: the kernel puts its surface pull near a fifth of a thousandth of a metre per second squared, and its escape velocity under one metre per second. Read that again — you could jog off this comet. Every intuition you built landing on the Moon, Mars, Venus and Titan now works against you: the hard part is not arriving. It is staying.
cur: 彗星67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko是一个山峰大小的天体，其重力微乎其微：它的表面重力约为千分之一米每平方秒，逃逸速度还不到每秒一米。再读一遍——你能慢跑离开这颗彗星。你在月球、火星、金星和泰坦着陆时建立的所有直觉现在都对你不利：难的不是到达，而是停留。

en: In November 2014, Philae arrived at 67P at about walking pace — and its anchoring harpoons failed to fire. What happens to an unanchored box that hits a world like this? It bounces. Set the rebound to about 38% of the touchdown speed and the point-mass energy equation sends Philae hundreds of metres back into space — a bounce that lasted nearly two hours. It stayed only because the rebound sat under 67P's escape velocity. One notch bouncier, and humanity's first comet landing would have been a slow-motion miss into the dark.
cur: 2014年11月，Philae以步行速度抵达67P——但其锚定鱼叉未能发射。一个无锚定的物体撞上这样的天体会怎样？它会反弹。将反弹速度设为约着陆速度的38%，点质量能量方程会将Philae送回数百米的太空——一次持续近两小时的反弹。它之所以留下来，只因反弹速度低于67P的逃逸速度。再弹一点，人类首次彗星着陆就会变成黑暗中的慢动作失手。

en: Now try the same class of bounce on Bennu — and the formula refuses to give you an apex, because there isn't one: the rebound clears Bennu's ~0.2 m/s escape velocity and simply leaves. This is not a bug to fix; it is the reason OSIRIS-REx never tried to land. Its TAG manoeuvre — Touch-And-Go — pressed a sampling arm into the rubble for about six seconds, fired thrusters, and backed away with the treasure. On a world you cannot stay on, the honest landing is the one that never pretends to stop.
cur: 现在对贝努尝试同样的反弹——公式拒绝给你顶点，因为没有顶点：反弹速度超过了贝努的逃逸速度（约0.2米/秒），直接飞离。这不是需要修复的错误；这正是OSIRIS-REx从不尝试着陆的原因。它的TAG机动——触及并离开——将采样臂按入碎屑约六秒，启动推进器，带着收获撤离。在你无法停留的天体上，诚实的着陆就是从不假装停止。

en: Hayabusa2 turned the bounce from a hazard into a vehicle. Its little MINERVA-II rovers had no wheels — on Ryugu, wheels would fling you off the ground you are trying to grip. Instead they carried internal torque wheels and HOPPED: a spin, a nudge of a tenth of a metre per second, a slow arc some fifteen metres downrange, and up to fifteen minutes of hang time before the next step. The first rovers ever to drive a world by deliberately, repeatedly leaving it.
cur: Hayabusa2 将弹跳从一个危险变成了一种行动方式。它的小型 MINERVA-II 漫游器没有轮子——在龙宫上，轮子会把你甩离你试图抓住的地面。相反，它们配备了内部扭矩轮，能够跳跃：一次旋转，一次十分之一米每秒的推动，一道缓慢的弧线向前跨越大约十五米，以及最多十五分钟的悬停时间才能进行下一步。这是历史上第一次有漫游器通过有意反复离开某个世界的方式来探测这个世界。

en: Itokawa is the smallest world on this ladder — a peanut of rubble a few hundred metres long, with an escape velocity you could beat with a firm push. In 2005 the first Hayabusa touched it, struggled, improvised, and still delivered the first asteroid dust ever returned to Earth, in 2010. Its samples confirmed something quietly profound: this 'mountain' is not a rock but a gravel pile, held together by a gravity ten-thousandth of yours.
cur: 糸川是这个序列中最小的天体——一颗花生般的碎石堆，长数百米，逃逸速度可用用力一推来超越。2005年第一颗Hayabusa触及它，艰难前行，临机应变，仍然成功送回了首批小行星尘埃，于2010年返回地球。其样本证实了一个深刻的事实：这座'山峰'不是岩石而是碎石堆，由重力加速度仅为地球十万分之一的引力粘合在一起。

en: Eros is the counterexample that proves the scale. At thirty-odd kilometres it is a giant among these worlds, and its ~10 m/s average escape velocity (ranging from roughly 3 to 17 m/s across its elongated surface) finally behaves like a place you can land. In 2001, NEAR Shoemaker — an orbiter with no landing legs at all — was eased down at under 2 m/s at mission's end and, to everyone's delight, kept transmitting from the surface for two weeks. On a small enough world, even a spacecraft that was never built to land can simply... arrive.
cur: 埃罗斯是证明尺度的反例。在三十多公里的范围内，它在这些世界中是一个巨人，其约10米/秒的平均逃逸速度（在其细长的表面上从大约3到17米/秒不等）终于表现得像一个可以着陆的地方。2001年，NEAR Shoemaker——一个根本没有着陆腿的轨道器——以不到2米/秒的速度在任务末期被缓缓放下，令所有人欣喜的是，它在表面继续传输信号长达两周。在足够小的世界上，即使是一艘从未为着陆而建造的航天器也能简单地...到达。

en: Five worlds, five firsts, three space agencies: ESA's Philae made the first comet landing (three touchdowns before it settled), JAXA's Hayabusa missions returned the first asteroid samples and hopped the first rovers across one, NASA's NEAR made the first asteroid landing and OSIRIS-REx the largest asteroid sample grab. Between them they wrote the manual for operating where gravity barely exists — the same physics every future asteroid miner and planetary-defence mission will live by.
cur: 五个世界，五次首创，三个航天机构：ESA的Philae实现了首次彗星着陆（三次接触后才稳定下来），JAXA的Hayabusa任务实现了首次小行星样本采集和首次在小行星上跳跃式巡视，NASA的NEAR实现了首次小行星着陆，OSIRIS-REx实现了最大规模的小行星样本采集。它们之间为在极弱重力环境中运作编写了规则手册——同样的物理学将指导每一个未来的小行星采矿任务和行星防御任务。

en: Philae's first bounce lasted nearly two hours. In that time it drifted about a kilometre — and the comet's gravity was so weak that mission control could not tell for hours whether it had landed or was drifting away forever.
cur: 菲莱的首次反弹持续了近两个小时。在这段时间里，它漂移了大约一公里——彗星的重力如此之弱，以至于任务控制中心在数小时内无法确定它是否着陆或者正在永远漂向远方。

en: No air at all, and a fierce dive down the Sun's gravity well. With nothing to brake against, every metre per second must be killed by the engine.
cur: 毫无空气，还要沿着太阳的引力井猛烈俯冲。无物可供刹车，每一米每秒都必须由发动机来抵消。

en: Start with the tool that tamed Mars, Venus and Titan: a parachute. On Mercury the formula refuses — there is no terminal velocity because there is essentially no air, just an exosphere thinner than a laboratory vacuum. Every landing trick that leans on an atmosphere — chutes, airbags slowed by drag, heat-shield braking — is paper here. Whatever speed you bring, you must cancel with a rocket. All of it.
cur: 从驯服火星、金星和土卫六的工具开始：降落伞。但水星上这套公式行不通——由于几乎没有空气，只有比实验室真空还稀薄的外大气层，所以不存在终端速度。任何依赖大气的着陆技巧——降落伞、气囊减速、热盾制动——在这里都成了废纸。无论你以何种速度到达，都必须用火箭完全抵消。全部。

en: Now feel the depth of the well. A 100-kilometre orbit above Mercury circles at about 2.9 kilometres per second — nearly twice the Moon's 1.6. Mercury may look like the Moon's grey twin, but it is a rocky heavyweight with an iron heart: more than twice the surface gravity, and every extra bit of orbital speed is speed a lander must later pay to shed.
cur: 现在感受引力井的深度吧。距水星表面100公里的轨道速度约为每秒2.9公里——几乎是月球1.6公里的两倍。水星看起来像月球的灰色孪生体，但它是个铁心重量级岩石：表面重力超过月球两倍多，每增加一点轨道速度，着陆器之后就要付出相应代价来消除这个速度。

en: Wire that orbital speed into the powered-descent burn and read the bill: with a thrust-to-weight of 3, stopping from Mercury orbit costs about 4.4 kilometres per second of Δv — cancel the orbit, then pay the gravity toll on the way down. For comparison, the same burn at the Moon costs about 2.4. Airless landing has no discounts: the planet does not brake you, ever.
cur: 把轨道速度代入动力下降燃烧，看看代价：推重比为3时，从水星轨道停止需要约每秒4.4公里的Δv——抵消轨道速度，然后在下降途中支付重力代价。相比之下，同样的燃烧在月球上只需约2.4公里。无大气着陆没有优惠：这个星球永远不会帮你减速。

en: Give your lander the same descent stage that conquered the Moon — Apollo-class, about 2.5 kilometres per second — and the verdict is blunt: roughly two kilometres per second short. This is the honest answer to a fair question: why has NOTHING ever landed on Mercury? Not because it is uninteresting, but because a Moon-lander's worth of rocket isn't half of what the job takes — and that is before you pay the years of gravity assists it costs merely to ARRIVE this deep in the Sun's well.
cur: 给你的着陆器配备征服月球的同级下降级——Apollo级，约每秒2.5公里——结果很直白：大约差两公里每秒。这是对一个公平问题的诚实回答：为什么从未有任何东西登陆水星？不是因为它不有趣，而是因为一个月球着陆器级别的火箭还不到所需的一半——这还没算上仅仅到达太阳井深处所需的数年引力助推成本。

en: No spacecraft has ever touched Mercury's surface. MESSENGER needed six planetary flybys over nearly seven years just to enter orbit, and ended its mission as an impact, not a landing. BepiColombo — ESA and JAXA's twin-orbiter mission — needed nine flybys and a cruise of more than eight years, arriving only in late 2026. The Lab's ladder shows why the surface itself remains unclaimed: it is one of the most expensive parking spots in the solar system.
cur: 没有航天器曾接触过水星表面。MESSENGER需要六次行星飞掠，花费近七年才进入轨道，其任务以撞击而非着陆结束。BepiColombo——ESA和JAXA的双轨道器任务——需要九次飞掠和超过八年的巡航，直到2026年晚些时候才抵达。实验室的阶梯显示为什么表面仍未被征服：它是太阳系中成本最高的停泊点之一。

en: When MESSENGER's fuel ran out in 2015, it hit Mercury at about 3.9 kilometres per second — adding a fresh crater to the planet it had mapped. Even its ending was a demonstration of the problem: without propellant, Mercury only knows one way down.
cur: 2015年MESSENGER燃料耗尽时，它以约每秒3.9公里的速度撞击水星——在它绘制的星球上增添了一个新陨石坑。即使它的结局也演示了问题所在：没有推进剂，水星只知道一种下降方式。

en: Every rocket is a bargain between thrust and efficiency. Compare the real engines that have flown, from kerosene workhorses to hydrogen upper stages, on the numbers that matter.
cur: 每一枚火箭都是推力与效率之间的权衡。从煤油主力到氢燃料上面级，用真正重要的数据来比较那些曾经飞过的真实发动机。

en: Three engines, one yardstick — the same card three times on purpose, so the numbers can be compared side by side. Start with the brute. The F-1 burned 2.6 tonnes of propellant a second to make 6.77 meganewtons — five of them lifted a Saturn V off the pad. But look past the thrust to the number beside it: specific impulse 304 seconds in vacuum (263 down at the pad), an exhaust velocity near 3 km/s. Thrust is what the pad demands. It is not what the journey rewards.
cur: 三台发动机,一把标尺——故意用同一张卡片三次,这样数字可以并排比较。从蛮力开始。F-1 每秒燃烧 2.6 吨推进剂,产生 677.7 万牛顿——五台发动机把土星五号送离发射台。但超越推力看另一个数字:真空中的比冲 304 秒(发射台处 263 秒),排气速度接近 3 km/s。推力是发射台的要求。它不是旅程所奖励的。

en: Now the surgeon. The RL10 makes about 100 kilonewtons — a fraction of a first-stage engine; it was never meant for the pad. But its hydrogen expander cycle reaches 450 seconds of specific impulse in modern variants (the first 1963 engine managed 427), an exhaust velocity of 4.4 km/s — every kilogram of propellant buys half again more speed. That is why versions of this quiet engine have flown upper stages from 1963 to this decade: upstairs, efficiency is the only currency.
cur: 现在轮到精密医生。RL10 产生约 100 千牛顿推力——仅为一级发动机的一小部分；它从不为发射台而设计。但其氢膨胀循环在现代型号中达到 450 秒比冲（首台 1963 年发动机达 427 秒），排气速度 4.4 公里/秒——每千克推进剂换来速度增加一倍半。这就是为什么这台静谧发动机的各种版本自 1963 年以来一直在飞行上面级，直到今年代：在高空，效率是唯一的货币。

en: Raptor is the modern attempt to refuse the choice. Full-flow staged combustion — both propellants fully gasified through twin preburners — holds methane at 350 seconds in vacuum (327 where the booster actually fires) while delivering booster-class thrust, in an engine built to be mass-produced and reflown. The trade between the F-1 and the RL10 didn't disappear; it got engineered thinner.
cur: Raptor 是现代的尝试，拒绝二选一。全流量分级燃烧——两种推进剂都经双预燃器完全汽化——在真空中保持甲烷 350 秒比冲（推进器实际工作处 327 秒），同时提供推进器级的推力，采用可大规模生产和重复使用的发动机。F-1 和 RL10 之间的权衡并未消失；只是被工程得更加精细。

en: Here is why the quiet number wins. Wire the RL10's specific impulse into the rocket equation at a mass ratio of ten and read the result: over 10 km/s from one stage. Run the same mass ratio with an F-1-class impulse and you get under 7. The only thing that changed is exhaust velocity — Isp·g0 is the lever the whole rocket equation swings on. One honest asterisk: in real vehicles hydrogen's low density buys some of this back in bigger tanks and heavier structure — which is why the brutes still own the first stage.
cur: 这就是为什么静谧的指标赢了。在质量比为 10 的条件下将 RL10 的比冲代入火箭方程，读出结果：单级超过 10 公里/秒。用 F-1 级的比冲跑同样的质量比，你得到不足 7 公里/秒。唯一改变的是排气速度——Isp·g0 是整个火箭方程摆动的杠杆。有一个实诚的注脚：在真实飞行器中，氢的低密度会导致更大的油箱和更重的结构——这就是为什么蛮力仍然统治着第一级。

en: The Lab's engine registry spans every major spacefaring agency — American gas-generators and staged-combustion, the Soviet RD line, Europe's Vulcain, China's YF engines, India's Vikas and CE-20, Japan's LE series. Each one is a different answer to the same question this ladder asks: how much of your thrust are you willing to trade for how much of your efficiency?
cur: 实验室的发动机注册表跨越所有主要航天机构——美国燃气发生器和分级燃烧发动机、苏联RD系列、欧洲的Vulcain、中国的YF系列、印度的Vikas和CE-20、日本的LE系列。每一台都是这个阶梯所问问题的不同答案：你愿意用多少推力换取多少效率？

cur: RL10 首次飞行于 1963 年，其后代至今仍在飞行——来自为真空而非发射台设计的发动机，六十年的服役生涯。

en: Now turn that momentum into a force. Hurl mass out the back at exhaust speed vₑ and, by Newton’s third law, the reaction pushes you forward: thrust F = ṁ·vₑ. This is the force the next step weighs against gravity.
cur: 现在把动量转化为力。以排气速度vₑ向后喷出质量，根据牛顿第三定律，反作用力将你向前推动：推力F = ṁ·vₑ。这就是下一步与重力相抗衡的力。

en: Momentum thrust only — ignores the nozzle pressure term
cur: 仅考虑动量推力——忽略喷管压力项

en: Load the rocket heavier — raise the loaded mass in the rocket equation until this verdict flips red. That mass is the payload wall for this stack.
cur: 加重火箭的负载——在火箭方程中提高装载质量，直到该判定变红。该质量就是这套火箭的有效载荷上限。

en: Push the payload up until a single stage can no longer reach orbit and the sizing wall appears — then watch staging beat it.
cur: 推高有效载荷，直到单级火箭无法再到达轨道并出现分级壁——然后观看分级火箭突破它。

en: Thin the parachute or the atmosphere until the touchdown stops being survivable. Mars leaves almost no margin — that is why it is hard.
cur: 减薄降落伞或大气，直到着陆不再可生存。火星几乎没有冗余——这就是为什么它很难。

en: Raise your approach speed until you bounce off instead of landing. On a world this small, escape velocity is barely walking pace.
cur: 提高接近速度，直到弹起而不是着陆。在这么小的星体上，逃逸速度只是步行速度。

en: Pour more Δv into a single rocket — can it clear the Sun on fuel alone, or do you still need the gravity-assist chain?
cur: 向单个火箭注入更多Δv——它能仅靠燃料越过太阳，还是仍需重力助推链？

en: Target: the 35,786 km geostationary altitude
cur: 目标：35,786 km 地球同步轨道高度

en: Newton’s second law: force (F) equals mass (m) times acceleration (a). The same push moves a lighter mass faster — this is the law every other rung here builds on.
cur: 牛顿第二定律：力(F)等于质量(m)乘以加速度(a)。相同的推力使较轻的质量加速更快——这是本处所有其他层级的基础定律。

en: Weight is just mass (m) pulled by gravity (g): W = m·g. Same mass, different world, different weight — which is why gravity is the field you pick.
cur: 重量就是质量(m)被重力(g)拉动：W = m·g。相同质量、不同世界、不同重量——这就是为什么重力是你选择的场。

en: Momentum is mass in motion: p = m·v. A rocket gains forward momentum by throwing exhaust backward — Newton’s third law, action and reaction, in numbers.
cur: 动量是运动中的质量：p = m·v。火箭通过向后喷射排气获得向前动量——牛顿第三定律，作用和反作用，用数字表示。

en: Thrust is the exhaust’s momentum per second: F = ṁ·vₑ (mass flow ṁ times exhaust speed vₑ). It turns the momentum idea from the last card into the force this rocket actually pushes with.
cur: 推力是排气每秒的动量：F = ṁ·vₑ(质量流ṁ乘以排气速度vₑ)。它将前一张卡片的动量概念转化为这枚火箭实际推动的力。

en: Thrust-to-weight ratio: TWR = T / W = T / (m·g). It weighs the thrust (previous card) against the weight (weight card). Above 1 it lifts off; below 1 it sits on the pad.
cur: 推重比：TWR = T / W = T / (m·g)。它将推力(前一张卡片)与重量(重量卡片)进行权衡。大于1时升空；小于1时留在发射台上。

en: The rocket equation. Δv is your speed budget — how much you can change your velocity. It grows with exhaust efficiency (Iₛₚ) and the wet/dry mass ratio m₀/m_f; the ln means every extra km/s costs exponentially more propellant.
cur: 火箭方程。Δv是你的速度预算——你能改变多少速度。它随排气效率(Iₛₚ)和湿质量/干质量比m₀/m_f增长；ln表示每额外增加1 km/s的成本呈指数增长推进剂。

en: Earth’s spin is a free head start: boost = v_eq·cosφ (the equator’s eastward speed times the cosine of your latitude φ). Maximum at the equator, zero at the poles — which is why launch sites hug the tropics.
cur: 地球自转是一次免费加速：助推 = v_eq·cosφ(赤道向东速度乘以纬度φ的余弦)。在赤道处最大，在两极处为零——这就是为什么发射场靠近热带。

en: Drop from height h and gravity does the rest: fall time t = √(2h/g), impact speed v = √(2gh). No thrust, no drag — gravity alone, the baseline every descent card fights against.
cur: 从高度 h 下落，重力完成其余工作：下落时间 t = √(2h/g)，撞击速度 v = √(2gh)。无推力、无阻力——仅重力作用，是每张下降卡对抗的基准。

en: Range R = v₀²·sin 2θ / g: launch speed v₀, launch angle θ, gravity g. The sin 2θ peaks at 45° — and the free-fall card already supplied the vertical half of this story.
cur: 射程 R = v₀²·sin 2θ / g：初速度 v₀、发射角 θ、重力加速度 g。sin 2θ 在 45° 时达峰值——自由落体卡已经提供了竖直分量。

en: The verdict as subtraction: margin = v_cap − v_req — what the rocket CAN do (Tsiolkovsky's rocket equation, from the launch lesson) minus what the mission needs. Positive means go; negative means redesign.
cur: 判断以减法表示：裕度 = v_cap − v_req——火箭能做到的（Tsiolkovsky火箭方程，来自发射课程）减去任务所需。正数意味着可行；负数意味着重新设计。

en: The real price of orbit: v_req = v_orbit + v_loss — the orbital speed itself plus everything the climb steals (gravity and drag). Orbit is a speed, and you must buy more than the sticker price.
cur: 轨道的真实代价：v_req = v_orbit + v_loss——轨道速度本身加上上升过程中的损耗（重力和阻力）。轨道是一种速度，你必须付出超过标价的代价。

en: margin = v_cap + v_boost − v_req: the rocket's Δv budget, plus the free eastward boost from Earth's spin (launch-site card), minus the cost of orbit. One line decides whether the design flies.
cur: 余量 = v_cap + v_boost − v_req：火箭的Δv预算，加上地球自转提供的向东免费助推（发射场卡），减去轨道成本。一个公式决定设计是否可行。

en: Tsiolkovsky run backwards: from payload m_pl, mass ratio R = e^(Δv/vₑ) and structure fraction ε, out comes the gross mass m₀ on the pad. The exponential is why big Δv means a huge rocket for a small payload.
cur: Tsiolkovsky 反向运算：从有效载荷 m_pl、质量比 R = e^(Δv/vₑ) 和结构系数 ε，得出垫板上的总质量 m₀。指数增长说明大Δv意味着为小有效载荷造超大火箭。

en: F = TWR·m₀·g₀: pick a thrust-to-weight ratio (TWR card), multiply by the gross mass the sizing card produced, and that is the thrust the pad must deliver. TWR > 1 or it never leaves.
cur: F = TWR·m₀·g₀：选择推重比（TWR卡），乘以规模卡得出的总质量，就是垫板需要提供的推力。TWR > 1，否则无法起飞。

en: N = ⌈F / F_engine⌉ — divide the thrust you need by the thrust one engine gives, and round UP. Fractional engines don't exist; the ceiling is why real rockets fly with 9, 27, 33 engines.
cur: N = ⌈F / F_engine⌉——需要的推力除以单个发动机推力，然后向上取整。分数个发动机不存在；取整是为什么真实火箭用 9、27、33 个发动机。

en: One stage tops out at vₑ·ln(1/ε) — even carrying nothing, the structure fraction ε caps its Δv. Divide the mission Δv by that ceiling and you get the number of stages you must drop along the way.
cur: 单级最高 vₑ·ln(1/ε)——即使不负载任何东西，结构系数 ε 也限制了Δv。任务Δv除以这个上限，得出沿途必须抛弃的级数。

en: N_b = ⌈(F_req − F_core)/F_b⌉: whatever thrust the core stage can't provide, strap-on boosters must — each adds F_b. Round up, because half a booster is not a thing.
cur: N_b = ⌈(F_req − F_core)/F_b⌉：核心级提不了的推力，由捆绑式助推器补足——每个加 F_b。向上取整，因为半个助推器不存在。

en: The cluster's total is simply F = N·F_engine, and the pad verdict is TWR = F/(m₀·g₀) — the engine-count card's N cashed back into the liftoff check.
cur: 集群总推力简单地是 F = N·F_engine，垫板判决是 TWR = F/(m₀·g₀)——发动机数卡的 N 兑现回起飞检查。

en: v = √(μ/r): circular-orbit speed from the body's gravity parameter μ and the orbit radius r. Lower orbits are FASTER — gravity pulls harder there, so the sideways speed must keep up.
cur: v = √(μ/r)：圆轨道速度由天体的引力参数 μ 和轨道半径 r 决定。低轨更快——重力拉力更大，横向速度必须跟上。

en: Vis-viva is the orbit's energy ledger: v = √(μ(2/r − 1/a)). At any point r on an orbit of semi-major axis a — half the ellipse's longest diameter — it hands you the speed; the circular-orbit card is just the special case a = r.
cur: 活力公式是轨道的能量账本：v = √(μ(2/r − 1/a))。在半长轴为 a 的轨道上的任意点 r — 椭圆最长直径的一半 — 它给出该处的速度；圆轨道是特殊情况，即 a = r。

en: The cheapest two-burn transfer: Δv = Δv₁ + Δv₂ — one burn stretches the orbit out, one circularizes at the top; both sizes come from vis-viva (previous card). Half an ellipse between two circles.
cur: 最便宜的两次烧组合：Δv = Δv₁ + Δv₂——一次烧把轨道拉高，一次在顶端圆化；两个大小都来自活力方程（前卡）。两圆之间的半椭圆。

en: Δv = v_orb·TWR/(TWR−1): killing orbital speed against gravity costs MORE than v_orb — while you brake, gravity keeps pulling. Weak engines (TWR barely above 1) pay a huge gravity tax.
cur: Δv = v_orb·TWR/(TWR−1)：对抗重力减速轨道速度代价超过 v_orb——减速过程中重力继续下拉。弱发动机（TWR 刚好大于 1）要付巨大的重力税。

en: The same Hohmann sum Δv = Δv₁ + Δv₂, one frame up: now the Sun's μ rules, the two circles are Earth's orbit and the target planet's, and the half-ellipse takes months to years.
cur: 同样的 Hohmann 求和 Δv = Δv₁ + Δv₂，上升一个尺度：现在太阳的 μ 主宰，两圆是地球轨道和目标行星轨道，半椭圆需要数月到数年。

en: 1/S = |1/T₁ − 1/T₂|: the synodic period S is how often two planets return to the same lineup — the beat frequency of their years. That beat sets how long you wait for the next cheap ride.
cur: 1/S = |1/T₁ − 1/T₂|：会合周期 S 是两颗行星回到同一排列的频率——它们年周期的拍频。这个拍频决定你等待下一次廉价转移需要多久。

en: Every departure date × flight time gets its price tag Δv(t_dep, t_of). The valleys of this map are the launch windows — the transfer and window cards, computed for every date at once.
cur: 每个发射日期 × 飞行时间都有价签 Δv(t_dep, t_of)。这幅图的谷底是发射窗口——转移和窗口卡，为每个日期同时计算。

en: A half-ellipse to the Moon: a = ½(r_LEO + r_Moon), flight time t_of = π√(a³/μ⊕). The same Hohmann geometry as the planet transfers — the Moon is just close enough to make it days, not months.
cur: 到月球的半椭圆：a = ½(r_LEO + r_Moon)，飞行时间 t_of = π√(a³/μ⊕)。与行星转移相同的 Hohmann 几何——月球足够近使其为天级而非月级。

en: The climb's full bill: Δv_needed = v_orbit + ℓ_grav + ℓ_drag + ℓ_steer. Each ℓ is speed the rocket burns without keeping — the gap between orbit's sticker price and what ascent really costs.
cur: 爬升的完整账单：Δv_needed = v_orbit + ℓ_grav + ℓ_drag + ℓ_steer。每个 ℓ 是火箭燃烧但没有保持的速度——轨道标价与爬升真实成本间的差距。

en: Linear-tangent steering: sin γ = A + B·t — the pitch angle's sine follows a straight line in time. Two constants steer the whole climb from vertical liftoff to horizontal orbit; that simplicity is why real guidance (PEG) uses it.
cur: 线性切线转向：sin γ = A + B·t — 俯仰角正弦随时间线性变化。两个常数控制从竖直起飞到水平轨道的整个上升段；这种简洁性正是实际制导（PEG）采用它的原因。

en: Follow the schedule v_target = min(v, g_sched·h): never fall faster than the height allows, never brake harder than a_max. Ride it down and you arrive at h = 0 with v ≈ 0 — a landing.
cur: 遵循目标速度计划 v_target = min(v, g_sched·h)：永远不要下降快于高度允许的速度，永远不要制动快于 a_max。按计划下降，你将以 h = 0、v ≈ 0 到达 — 着陆。

en: Rolling the capsule banks its lift: cos φ is the command. Lift up stretches the path (shallower, cooler); lift down bends it in — the flight angle γ answers to L/D and the bank. Steering with no engine at all.
cur: 滚转胶囊舱倾斜升力：cos φ 是指令。升力向上拉长轨迹（更浅、更冷）；升力向下弯入 — 飞行角 γ 受 L/D 和倾角影响。完全无发动机的转向。

en: Range answers one-way to bank — more lift-up, more range. A monotone knob can be bisected: solve cos φ so the landed range hits R_target. That is how a capsule lands on a dot.
cur: 射程单向响应倾角 — 更多向上升力，更远的射程。一个单调旋钮可被二分法求解：求 cos φ 使着陆射程击中 R_target。这是胶囊舱在一个点上着陆的方式。

en: v_t = √(2mg/(ρ·A·C_d)): fall fast enough and drag equals weight — speed locks at v_t. Heavier m falls faster; a bigger chute area A or thicker air ρ slows the fall. Weight = m·g is the numerator (from the launch lesson).
cur: v_t = √(2mg/(ρ·A·C_d))：下落足够快时，阻力等于重力——速度锁定在v_t。更重的物体m下落更快；更大的降落伞面积A或更稠密的空气ρ会减慢下落。重力 = m·g是分子（来自发射课程）。

en: margin = v_safe − v_t: what the landing gear survives minus what the parachute delivers (terminal-velocity card). Positive: touchdown. Negative: you need retro-rockets or airbags — the next cards.
cur: 裕度 = v_safe − v_t:起落架能承受的速度减去降落伞实际带来的速度(见"终端速度"卡片)。为正:可以着陆。为负:就需要反推火箭或气囊——见后面的卡片。

en: The blunt check v_impact ≤ v_airbag: can the bags absorb the leftover speed? This eats a crash rather than preventing one — how Pathfinder and the MER rovers reached Mars soil.
cur: 钝体检查 v_impact ≤ v_airbag：充气囊能吸收剩余速度吗？这是缓冲撞击而不是阻止它 — Pathfinder 和 MER 到达火星表面的方式。

en: Δv_retro = v_t − v_safe: the speed gap the parachute cannot close, killed by rockets in the final seconds. It is exactly the soft-landing margin, sign-flipped into a burn.
cur: Δv_retro = v_t − v_safe：降落伞无法弥补、最后时刻由火箭消除的速度差。它正是软着陆 margin，符号翻转后的燃烧。

en: Δv = v_circ − v_apo: brake on one side of the orbit and the OTHER side drops into the atmosphere. A small burn now — then drag does the expensive half of the work.
cur: Δv = v_circ − v_apo：在轨道一侧制动，另一侧下沉进大气。现在小小燃烧 — 然后阻力承担昂贵的一半工作。

en: Entry banks E = ½v² of energy per kilogram into heat; the peak deceleration a_peak = v²·sinγ/(2eH) follows how steeply (γ) you dive through the atmosphere's scale height H. Steeper means a harder slam.
cur: 大气再入将 E = ½v² 每千克能量转化为热；峰值减速度 a_peak = v²·sinγ/(2eH) 取决于你穿过大气标度高度 H 的陡峭度（γ）。更陡意味着更猛烈的冲击。

en: Squeezed from both sides: the perigee r_p = a(1−e) must dip into the atmosphere (or you skip off into space), but the slam a_peak grows with entry angle (or you burn up). The survivable range of γ is a corridor a few degrees wide.
cur: 受两侧挤压：近地点 r_p = a(1−e) 必须深入大气（否则你反弹入太空），但撞击 a_peak 随再入角增加（否则你烧毁）。可生存的 γ 范围是宽度仅几度的走廊。

en: Little worlds, little pull: g = μ/R² and v_esc = √(2μ/R). On a comet both are tiny — walking speed beats escape velocity, which is why landing there is really docking.
cur: 小天体，小引力：g = μ/R² 和 v_esc = √(2μ/R)。在彗星上两者都很小 — 步行速度超过逃逸速度，这就是为什么登陆那里实际上是对接。

en: Touch down at v_td and the surface gives back v_b = e·v_td (restitution e). In micro-gravity (this goal's opening card) that bounce can arc kilometres high — Philae's double bounce, as an equation.
cur: 在v_td速度接触表面，表面反弹速度v_b = e·v_td（恢复系数e）。在微重力环境下（本目标的开局卡牌），这样的反弹可以弧形上升数公里——菲莱彗星着陆器的双次反弹，用方程表示。

en: vₑ = Iₛₚ·g₀: specific impulse converts straight into exhaust speed. It is the efficiency knob inside Tsiolkovsky — double the Iₛₚ and every kilogram of propellant buys twice the Δv.
cur: vₑ = Iₛₚ·g₀：比冲直接转换为排气速度。它是 Tsiolkovsky 方程内的效率旋钮 — 把 Iₛₚ 翻倍，每千克推进剂就能买到两倍的 Δv。

en: Escape from the Sun at distance r: v_esc = √(2μ☉/r) — exactly √2 times the circular speed there. That √2 is the whole story: leaving costs 41% more speed than orbiting.
cur: 在距离 r 处逃离太阳：v_esc = √(2μ☉/r) — 恰好是那里圆周速度的 √2 倍。这个 √2 就是全部故事：离开需要比环绕快 41% 的速度。

en: Δv = v_esc − v_orb: you already MOVE at Earth's orbital speed around the Sun — escaping only costs the difference. Starting from a moving platform is most of the discount.
cur: Δv = v_esc − v_orb：你已经以地球绕太阳的公转速度在运动 — 逃逸只需额外的差速。从运动平台起飞获得了大部分折扣。

en: Burn deep in Earth's gravity well: Δv = √(v∞² + v_esc²) − v_circ. Fuel spent where you move fastest buys the same v∞ for less — the Oberth effect, the cheapest exit there is.
cur: 在地球重力井深处燃烧：Δv = √(v∞² + v_esc²) − v_circ。在你运动最快处消耗燃料，相同的 v∞ 花费更少 — Oberth 效应，最便宜的离开方式。

en: A flyby is elastic in the planet's frame — speed in equals speed out. Swing through a full 180° and your velocity relative to the planet reverses, which adds up to Δv_max = 2v∞ in the Sun's frame. Free speed for the spacecraft; the planet pays with a recoil too tiny to measure.
cur: 在行星参考系中，飞掠是弹性碰撞 — 进入速度等于射出速度。如果穿过整个180°的轨迹，你相对行星的速度会反向，在太阳参考系中这相当于 Δv_max = 2v∞。航天器获得免费速度增益；行星付出的反冲太微小而无法测量。

en: margin = v_cap + v_assist − v_req: the rocket's budget plus what flybys donate (gravity-assist card), against the price of leaving the Sun. Voyager's ledger in one line.
cur: margin = v_cap + v_assist − v_req：火箭的预算加上飞掠捐献（重力辅助卡）对抗离开太阳的代价。旅行者的账目在一行里。

en: Chain the flybys and the donations add: Δv_max ≤ Σ 2v∞ᵢ — each planet contributes its 2v∞ (gravity-assist card). This sum is how spacecraft reach speeds no rocket alone could buy.
cur: 链接飞掠，捐献相加：Δv_max ≤ Σ 2v∞ᵢ — 每颗行星贡献其 2v∞（重力辅助卡）。这个和数是航天器达到单火箭无法买到的速度的方式。

en: Illuminated fraction k = ½(1 + cos α): the phase angle α between Sun and Moon, seen from Earth, sets how much face is lit. New at α = 180°, full at 0° — geometry, not Earth's shadow.
cur: 光照分数 k = ½(1 + cos α)：相位角 α 是从地球看太阳与月球之间的夹角，决定了月面被照亮的部分。新月时 α = 180°，满月时 0° — 纯几何，不是地球的影子。

en: Apparent size ∝ 1/d: the Moon's elliptical orbit takes it near (perigee) and far (apogee), so its disc swells and shrinks by about 14%. A 'supermoon' is just perigee timed with full phase.
cur: 视角大小 ∝ 1/d：月球椭圆轨道使其在近地点和远地点间运动，圆盘因此胀缩约 14%。'超级月亮'只是近地点恰好与满月同时发生。

en: The Moon's orbit tilts 5°, so its shadow usually misses. Only when the Moon sits within |β| < 1.5° of the ecliptic at new or full can an eclipse happen — the twice-a-year eclipse seasons.
cur: 月球轨道倾斜 5°，月影通常偏离地球。只有月球在新月或满月时位于黄道 |β| < 1.5° 范围内时才会发生食 — 一年两次的食季。

en: How high the Moon culminates: h_max = 90° − |φ − δ| — your latitude φ against the Moon's declination δ. The same rule the Sun obeys; it is why the full Moon rides high in winter.
cur: 月球的南中高度：h_max = 90° − |φ − δ| — 你的纬度 φ 对月球赤纬 δ。太阳也遵循同样规则；这就是为什么满月在冬季高挂天空。

en: One radius, two numbers: v = √(μ/r) and T = 2π√(r³/μ) (orbital-velocity card plus Kepler's third law). LEO laps Earth in 90 minutes; higher orbits slow — the whole regime map in two formulas.
cur: 一个半径，两个公式：v = √(μ/r) 和 T = 2π√(r³/μ)（轨道速度加开普勒第三定律）。近地轨道绕地球一圈 90 分钟；更高轨道速度更慢 — 整个轨道体系由两个公式决定。

en: Set the period T to one sidereal day and solve Kepler: a = ∛(μT²/4π²) — 35,786 km up, the orbit keeps pace with the turning Earth. Hang there and you stand still in the sky.
cur: 将周期 T 设为一个恒星日，求解开普勒定律：a = ∛(μT²/4π²) — 距地面 35,786 km，轨道与地球自转保持同步。悬停其中，你在天空中静止不动。

en: Light speed is the toll: Δt = 2h/c for the round trip. LEO answers in milliseconds; GEO's 36,000 km costs a quarter of a second — why voice over GEO feels laggy.
cur: 光速是代价：Δt = 2h/c 用于往返。近地轨道响应以毫秒计；地球同步轨道 36,000 km 的距离花费四分之一秒 — 这就是为什么地球同步轨道上的语音传输感觉滞后。

en: Earth's equatorial bulge (J₂) twists orbit planes. Choose the inclination i where that twist makes exactly one lap per year and your orbit keeps pace with the Sun — the same local time under every pass. Sun-synchronous.
cur: 地球赤道隆起（J₂）扭转轨道平面。选择倾角 i 使这种扭转每年精确进行一圈，轨道与太阳保持同步 — 每次经过下方时本地时间相同。太阳同步轨道。

en: The bulge also swings an orbit's low point around the orbit. At 5cos²i − 1 = 0 — i = 63.4° — the swing stops and the ellipse freezes in orientation: Molniya's trick for keeping its slow, high APOGEE dwelling over the far north.
cur: 重力摄动也会使轨道的近地点绕轨道摆动。当 5cos²i − 1 = 0 — 即 i = 63.4° 时，摆动停止，椭圆轨道方向冻结：这是 Molniya 卫星使用的技巧，使其缓慢、高远地点的卫星能长时间停留在高北纬上空。

en: One satellite sees a cap of half-angle λ = arccos(R·cos ε/(R+h)) − ε: altitude h buys footprint, the elevation mask ε shrinks it. Divide the circle by the cap and you get the ring count — constellation math.
cur: 一颗卫星可见一个半角为 λ = arccos(R·cos ε/(R+h)) − ε 的圆冠：高度 h 决定覆盖范围，仰角掩模 ε 缩小它。用圆周除以圆冠就得到星座需要的卫星数 — 星座数学。

en: cos A = cos i / cos φ: to reach inclination i from latitude φ, aim at azimuth A. You cannot launch to an inclination below your latitude — the equation itself refuses (|cos A| ≤ 1).
cur: cos A = cos i / cos φ：从纬度 φ 到达倾角 i，射向方位角 A。不能发射到低于纬度的倾角 — 方程本身禁止了（|cos A| ≤ 1）。

en: While you fly one orbit (period T), Earth turns beneath you: each ground track shifts west by Δλ = 360°·T/T⊕. It is why one satellite sweeps the whole planet without steering.
cur: 当你飞完一圈（周期 T）时，地球在下方转动：每条地面轨迹西移 Δλ = 360°·T/T⊕。这就是为什么一颗卫星可以扫过整个地球而无需转向。

en: From altitude h the horizon dips by θ = arccos(R/(R+h)) — the slice of Earth a satellite can see, and the slice of sky where a pass can happen at all.
cur: 从高度 h 地平线下沉角度 θ = arccos(R/(R+h)) — 卫星能看到的地球扇形，也是经过可以发生的天空扇形。

en: No closed formula here: propagate the live TLE forward and find the next time the ISS climbs above 10° at your site. The visibility-window card said a pass exists — this one says WHEN.
cur: 没有闭形式公式：传播实时 TLE 并找到国际空间站在你的位置上升超过 10° 的下一时刻。可见窗口卡说明有经过 — 这张卡说明何时。

en: Elongation ε = λ_planet − λ☉: the angle between a planet and the Sun in our sky. It decides everything about viewing — near 0° the planet is lost in glare, near 180° it is up all night.
cur: 离角 ε = λ_planet − λ☉：行星与太阳在我们天空中的夹角。它决定了观测的一切 — 接近 0° 行星淹没在眩光中，接近 180° 则整晚可见。

en: An inner planet can only swing so far from the Sun: ε_max = arcsin(a(1+e)) — the arcsin of its APHELION distance in AU, the farthest its orbit reaches. Venus caps near 47° (aphelion 0.73 AU), Mercury near 28° (aphelion 0.47 AU) — why both are forever morning or evening stars.
cur: 内行星只能在距太阳一定范围内摆动：ε_max = arcsin(a(1+e)) — 其远日点距离（天文单位）的反正弦值，即其轨道能到达的最远处。金星的最大角距约 47°（远日点 0.73 AU），水星约 28°（远日点 0.47 AU） — 这就是为何两者永远只能是晨星或昏星。

en: Retrograde is an overtake, not a reversal: as Earth laps an outer planet, the planet's apparent drift λ̇ along the ecliptic turns negative for a while. This card computes today's rate — negative means the loop is under way.
cur: 逆行是一次追赶，不是反转：当地球超越外行星时，行星沿黄道的视运动 λ̇ 短暂转为负值。此卡计算今日速率 — 负值意味着逆行环正在进行。

en: Culmination height h_max = 90° − |φ − δ|: your latitude φ against the planet's declination δ (the moon-altitude card's rule, aimed at planets). It says how high tonight's target ever gets — low means mud and haze.
cur: 南中高度 h_max = 90° − |φ − δ|：你的纬度 φ 对行星赤纬 δ（月球高度卡的规则，应用于行星）。说明目标今晚的最大高度 — 低意味着泥泞和薄雾。
